ouray|2026-11-17|Board of County Commiss: A substantive session for the Ouray County BOCC. Two resolutions stand out: Resolution 2026-031 repeals the county's austerity measures (Resolution 2026-008), signaling a shift in the county's fiscal posture; and Resolution 2026-032 adopts a formal AI policy and governance standards — one of the first such moves in the region. The 2027 budget gets an update and discussion, followed by a public hearing on amending the 2026 budget via Resolution 2026-033. On the infrastructure side, commissioners take up a change order on the Corbett Creek project, a runoff concern on CR-361's upper bridge, and an OHV grant application for an Alpine Ranger Program through Colorado Parks and Wildlife. Human Services business includes MOUs with CASA and an IGA with Montrose County for child support services. Executive session covers active water and civil litigation — dockets dating back to 2019 — plus potential code enforcement action for unpermitted structures and road closures in the McIntyre Gulch high alpine area, and a possible property transaction at 800 N. Oak Street in Ouray.

telluride|2026-12-02|Ecology Commission: The Ecology Commission takes up a proposed ordinance that would phase out combustion-powered lawn and garden equipment townwide — first for leaf blowers by January 1, 2028, then for all other covered equipment (mowers, trimmers, edgers, and the like) by January 1, 2030. The draft ordinance would also immediately bar the Town from purchasing any new gas-powered lawn equipment. Snow removal gear, chainsaws, portable generators, and wildfire/defensible-space work are carved out. Enforcement would run complaint-based, with a written warning on a first offense; commercial operators can be cited both individually and as a business entity. Colorado's HB23-1161 point-of-sale discount and San Miguel Power Association rebates together could offset roughly half the cost of replacement equipment. This is a work session — no vote is on the table yet — with the path forward likely running through a Town Council agenda item after today's discussion.
